subject: Interim egress waiver & subprocessor rotation request
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@healthlytics.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@healthlytics.com>
Date: 2025-05-17T08:32:00Z
Subject: Data residency question — temporary egress waiver & subprocessor rotation

Hi Aisha / Priyom,

We’re finalizing the security checklist for the Proof-of-Concept and have a couple of asks from our DPO/legal: would Redwood be able to support a short, scheduled rotation of analytics processing to an EU-only subprocessor for a 48-hour window during our EU go-live? We need to understand: 

- What exactly constitutes a “temporary egress” event in your platform (network transfer vs cached/replicated tokens).
- Whether Redwood can sequence a rotation so analytics requests hit an EU-only infra pool for a defined window and then revert automatically.
- What evidence you can provide (subprocessor roster snapshot, packet/audit logs, KMS attestations) and the lead time for those artifacts.

This is sensitive for us because some test PHI-like records will be included in the POC. If rotation is technically possible, please outline required steps, potential SLA impact, and any paperwork (DPA addendum/DocuSign) we need to sign.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if easier.

Best,
Nina Patel
Head of Security, HealthyLytics
Attachments: compliance-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@healthlytics.com>, Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@healthlytics.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2025-05-17T10:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Data residency question — temporary egress waiver & subprocessor rotation

Nina — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary of what we can provide and next steps: 

1) Definition & scope
- Temporary egress: any outbound transfer of tokens or model-cached data from the EU-bound serving pool to a non-EU region for processing. This includes short-lived KV cache replication used for burst capacity.

2) Proposed operational approach
- We can schedule a 48-hour "EU-only analytics" window by routing analytics routes to an EU-dedicated pool and pinning requests for that time. We’ll avoid cross-region replica promotion during the window.
- Fallback: if EU capacity is saturated, we will fail closed for analytics routes (return 429/503 with retry guidance) unless you opt into a conditional failover.

3) Evidence we can supply
- Subprocessor roster snapshot for the period (CSV), SOC 2 attestations for supporting subprocessors, and a signed DPA addendum via DocuSign.
- Audit logs: request-level routing decisions and KMS key usage logs (redacted) for the window.

4) Paperwork & timing
- We can prepare a DPA addendum and DocuSign link; signature to confirm the rotation. Expect 3–5 business days to prepare artifacts once scope is agreed.

I’ve attached a proposed rotation timeline (proposed-rotation-timeline.xlsx) and looped in Priyom for feasibility and runbook items. If that looks good we can surface the DocuSign link and a short runbook for ops handoff.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0198
Attachments: proposed-rotation-timeline.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Subject: Re: Data residency question — temporary egress waiver & subprocessor rotation

Nina / Aisha — quick technical note from infra/ops: we can execute the flow Aisha described with these caveats and steps.

Planned sequence (high level):
- T-72h: Provision EU analytics pool and create ephemeral routing rule pinned to account/route.
- T-24h: Warm KV cache with non-sensitive prompts to avoid cold-start amplification.
- T-1h: Enable strict routing policy (route:analytics) -> EU pool; set cache TTL and disable cross-region replication for the flagged routes.
- Window (48h): Monitor request-level latency and KMS operations; stream audit logs to the signed S3 bucket (read-only).
- T+1h after window: Revert routing policy and re-enable normal replication.

Operational notes: 
- KMS: we’ll generate a short-lived envelope key for the window; we can provide key-use logs but not raw key material. If you require split KMS (customer-held), we’ll need an additional onboarding step.
- SLA impact: if you choose the "fail closed" posture we expect a potential ~0.5–2% increase in 5xx when traffic spikes (because we won’t route to non-EU fallback). If you allow conditional failover to non-EU for low-priority analytics, impact is negligible.

Attachments: ephemeral-egress-runbook.pdf (runbook stub) — contains step-by-step commands and post-window verification checklist.

I can be the technical SPOC for execution day.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Infrastructure Ops, Redwood Inference
Internal: #ops-runbooks

Aisha / Priyom — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear runbook. A few follow-ups from the DPO/legal side before we sign anything: 

- Can you confirm the exact retention window for the audit logs you’ll provide (we prefer 90 days immutable export for POC data).
- Please confirm whether the ephemeral envelope key usage logs contain full request IDs or only hashed request identifiers (we need pseudonymous linkage).
- We need a clear SLA note describing the expected degradation if we choose fail-closed vs allow conditional failover (numbers you cited are fine; please put them in the DPA addendum).

If you can attach the DocuSign link for the DPA addendum and the runbook + timeline in one bundle I’ll route to legal for expedited review. Also please confirm Priyom is the SPOC for the operation day.

Regards,
Nina Patel
Head of Security, HealthyLytics
